gen_risks.description: Generation and improper management of medical, chemical, and hazardous laboratory waste resulting from expanded diagnostic testing and laboratory operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement national Healthcare Waste Management Plans, provide specialized waste handling equipment, and train laboratory personnel in biosafety and biosecurity protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: Low interoperability and technical fragmentation among human, animal, and environmental health information systems preventing real-time One Health disease surveillance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy interoperable digital surveillance platforms, establish standardized data-sharing protocols, and integrate CAHIS and COHIS with DHIS2.
gen_risks.evidence: gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities, disease surveillance and information systems, supply chain infrastructure and management

gen_risks.description: Insufficient domestic budgetary allocations and fiscal space leading to post-project financial unsustainability of health security operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, establish dedicated budget line items, and explore public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: low government funding (driven by weak revenue generation and low prioritization of health in the government's budget)

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary risks and questionable expenditures in decentralized, local-level project activities such as remote trainings and workshops.
gen_risks.mitigation: Customize financial management manuals, enforce strict expenditure verification protocols, and deploy internal audit oversight for subnational activities.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays and limited market competition for complex medical goods, laboratory equipment, and civil works contracts in fragile settings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early market engagement, deploy experienced procurement specialists, utilize STEP real-time tracking, and explore joint regional procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting required PIU specialists and fulfilling legal financial covenants post-effectiveness, slowing implementation start.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated PIUs early, utilize project preparation advances where available, and closely track legal covenant compliance windows.
gen_risks.evidence: Recruit an accountant, a knowledge management and communication specialist, a monitoring and evaluation specialist... not later than one month

gen_risks.description: Risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) stemming from labor influx and increased community health workforce deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, enforce codes of conduct, and establish survivor-centered grievance channels.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... create concerns of Sexual exploitation

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable, marginalized, or remote populations (including IDPs, refugees, rural women, and indigenous communities) from health security interventions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Customize Stakeholder Engagement Plans to local languages and contexts, mandate inclusive outreach targets, and deploy mobile health teams.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to... the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Ongoing armed conflict, civil unrest, and security threats in FCV regions disrupting project delivery and restricting physical access.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formulate site-specific Security Risk Assessments and Security Management Plans, utilize flexible implementation modalities, and coordinate with local actors.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements

gen_risks.description: Delays in negotiating and executing key inter-institutional agreements and regulatory frameworks, such as the CEMAC MoU with WOAH.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated legal/inter-institutional focal points, set strict deadline tracking for MoU execution, and maintain frequent RCC dialogue.
gen_risks.evidence: enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (the 'MoU') with the WOAH under the terms and in a form and substance satisfactory

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate shocks (flooding, extreme heat) damaging healthcare infrastructure and exacerbating climate-sensitive vector/waterborne disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply EDGE level 1 green/resilient building standards to facility refurbishments, integrate climate alerts into early warning systems, and deploy solar energy.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters registered in Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC

gen_risks.description: Occupational health hazards and environmental nuisances (dust, noise, construction waste) during health facility and laboratory civil refurbishments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), enforce worker PPE usage, and manage construction waste disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: potential impacts related to construction, upgrades... occupational health and safety risks... management and disposal of hazardous materials

gen_risks.description: Breakdown in multi-sectoral One Health coordination among human, animal, and environmental government ministries and agencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize national and subnational One Health coordination platforms, formalize inter-ministerial Steering Committees, and execute joint simulation drills.
gen_risks.evidence: gaps are primarily due to limited domestic and regional resources, weak institutional capacities... and insufficient multisectoral coordination.

gen_risks.description: Gender imbalances and technical workforce shortages in disease surveillance, field epidemiology, and laboratory operations in underserved areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted FETP/ISAVET scholarships for women, implement gender targets (30%+ female trainees), and offer flexible training modules.
gen_risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making... underrepresentation in key technical roles

gen_risks.description: Massive influxes of refugees and internally displaced persons straining local health infrastructure and disease surveillance systems in border zones.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen surveillance and health service capacity at Points of Entry, deploy mobile health units, and coordinate with humanitarian response platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: Chad currently hosts over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees due to conflict in Lake Chad Basin and instability in Sudan

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
